slides.title: Principle and source
bullets: Proteins give an intense violet-blue complex with copper salts in alkaline medium; iodide is included as an antioxidant.
The colour intensity is proportional to the total protein concentration in the sample.
High protein — in haemoconcentration (dehydration); low protein — in haemodilution, impaired synthesis, loss (haemorrhage) or excessive catabolism.

slides.title: Principle and source
bullets: This protocol follows, as an example, the instructions for use of the SPINREACT “Total Protein” kit (IFU BSIS30-I, 08/11/22). The IFU of your laboratory’s own kit always takes precedence: other kits may use different volumes, times, factors and reference values.

slides.title: Specimen, reagents and equipment
bullets: Specimen: serum or heparinised plasma — stable for 1 month refrigerated (2–8 °C).
Biuret reagent: sodium potassium tartrate 15 mmol/L, sodium iodide 100 mmol/L, potassium iodide 5 mmol/L, copper (II) sulphate 5 mmol/L, sodium hydroxide 1000 mmol/L.
Standard: bovine albumin, 7 g/dL (primary standard).

slides.title: Specimen, reagents and equipment
bullets: Equipment: spectrophotometer or analyser reading at 540 nm, 1.0 cm cuvettes.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: The reagent and standard are ready to use — no dilution or mixing is needed.
Store the kit at 2–8 °C protected from light until expiry.
Signs of deterioration: particles, turbidity or blank absorbance at 540 nm ≥ 0.22.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: IFU: calibration with the aqueous standard may cause a systematic error in automatic procedures — a serum calibrator is then recommended.
The values come from the SPINREACT “Total Protein” IFU (BSIS30-I). The IFU of the kit you use and the analyser manual always take precedence — check the programme against them.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 1. Conditions: wavelength 540 nm (530–550); temperature 37 °C or 15–25 °C.
2. Use a 1 cm cuvette; zero the instrument with distilled water.
3. Pipette into a cuvette: blank — reagent 1.0 mL; standard — reagent 1.0 mL + standard 25 µL; sample — reagent 1.0 mL + sample 25 µL.
4. Mix and incubate: 5 min at 37 °C or 10 min at room temperature.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 5. Read the absorbance (A) of the sample and standard against the blank; the colour is stable for at least 30 minutes.

slides.title: Semi-automatic analyser: total protein programme
rows: 5 min at 37 °C or 10 min at room temperature
Sample and standard — against the reagent blank

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: Result (g/dL) = (A sample − A blank) / (A standard − A blank) × 7 (standard concentration).
Linear up to 14 g/dL; above that, dilute the sample 1/2 with NaCl 9 g/L and multiply the result by 2.
IFU reference: adults 6.6–8.3 g/dL; newborns 5.2–9.1 g/dL.

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: These values are for orientation; each laboratory should establish its own reference range.

slides.title: Interferences and errors
bullets: Haemoglobin and lipaemia interfere — assess haemolysed or lipaemic samples.
The standard is easily contaminated — use clean disposable tips.
IFU: calibration with the aqueous standard may cause a systematic error in automatic procedures — a serum calibrator is then recommended.
Drugs and other interfering substances are listed in the literature (IFU — Young DS).
IFU: performance depends on the analyser used.

slides.title: Quality control
bullets: Assayed control sera are run with each series (IFU: SPINTROL H Normal and Pathologic).
If a control falls outside its range, check the instrument, reagents and calibrator; do not release patient results.
Each laboratory sets its own quality-control scheme and the corrective actions when controls are out of tolerance.

slides.title: Safety
bullets: Biuret reagent: H314 — causes severe skin burns and eye damage.
Serum and plasma are potentially infectious: wear gloves and never pipette by mouth.
Follow the precautions in the IFU and the safety data sheet (SDS) when handling the reagents.
Used cuvettes, tubes and tips are disinfected.
